title: Earth's core is as hot as the Sun's surface
body: Seismic waves and laboratory melting experiments put the inner core near 5,000-6,000 kelvin, comparable to the Sun's visible surface, yet it stays solid because pressure there exceeds three million atmospheres. The core is crystallising over geological time, and that freezing helps power the magnetic dynamo shielding the surface.
source_hint: Core temperature estimates (Alfe et al., mineral physics)
